value.rationale: PASS: The smallest odd prime-square cyclic example after C9 where the elementary support-product bound permits a strictly smaller sum, C25, is a natural first obstruction to extrapolating prime sine-matrix full-spark results. The sharp value fourteen rules out the allowable support-sum twelve patterns and completely determines all four projective equality classes, providing a concrete non-field benchmark for symmetry-refined finite Fourier uncertainty and future prime-square conjectures. The result is neither a renamed textbook inequality nor a chosen arbitrary narrow parameter; its full exact extremizer census is not implied by known general bounds.
